newsitem.title: USA: Ill. GOP leaders weighing school funding - papers.
newsitem.headline: Ill. GOP leaders weighing school funding - papers.

text.p: Illinois Republican lawmakers are questioning their governor's school funding plan, which calls for increasing the state income tax to boost aid to schools and also provide some property tax cuts, Chicago newspapers reported Friday.
Republican Gov. Jim Edgar has proposed raising the state income tax from 3 percent to 3.75 percent to provide additional school funding and $1.2 billion in property tax cuts.
Suburban Republican lawmakers question whether the swap is necessary or would surrender local control over school funding, the Chicago Tribune reported.
Furthermore, lawmakers are concerned that the property tax cuts will be temporary only, the Chicago Sun-Times reported.

A group of suburban lawmakers believes boosting taxes on cigarettes and riverboat gambling and adding taxes to junk food and voice mail could generate $350 million, enough to raise funding for the poorest schools to an acceptable level, the Sun-Times reported.
A panel of eight legislators has been assembled to develop a school funding plan before the end of the General Assembly's Spring session in three weeks.
